kept.what: Final messages say Kavya and Kevin 'both love live music and trivia' and Kevin and Quinn 'both love pickleball and baseball' [322].
kept.why: Kevin only 'really likes' live music and is 'up for' trivia; Quinn only 'really likes' baseball, so the intensity is overstated.
kept.expected: Shared interests described at the strength the profiles give.
kept.fix: Change 'both love' to 'both enjoy' or similar.

kept.what: The invitation to Kevin claims the venue is 'close to home' [232].
kept.why: Kevin avoids long drives and no profile or event data states where Ten Trails is relative to Lawson Hills, so the claim is unsupported by the log.
kept.expected: Only state proximity if known from the data.
kept.fix: Drop 'close to home' or state the actual location.

kept.what: Quinn's agent justified its yes with Quinn's 'love of running' [259].
kept.why: The profile lists running under 'really likes', not 'loves'; a slight overstatement, though the decision is still correct.
kept.expected: Reasons that mirror the profile's stated strength.

kept.what: The matchmaker told Isabel 'your dog is welcome' [287].
kept.why: Her profile lists 'dog walks' as an interest but nowhere says she owns a dog; the log also gives no basis for the trail's dog policy.
kept.expected: Mention only what the profile supports, e.g. that it is a dog-walk-style outing or that dogs are allowed if known.
kept.fix: Change 'your dog is welcome' to 'dogs are welcome'.

kept.what: The group was planned and locked at only 2 people while Grace C. (hiking 3, keenness 3, overlaps on baseball and watch sports) sat unasked in the break room [199][313].
kept.why: A two-person group is fragile and Grace appears at least as compatible as either member, though the log does not show why she was excluded.
kept.expected: Consider inviting the keenest compatible break-room member to reach three.
kept.fix: Ask Grace C. as a third before locking.

kept.what: Pitches and confirmations generalised interests beyond the profiles: Chris was told the other three parents are 'into baking' though Imani lists no baking, and Imani's confirmation says Chris loves coffee though he is only 'up for' it.
kept.why: Final and pitch messages should use only facts from the profiles; small overstatements set slightly wrong expectations.
kept.expected: Describe shared interests only where the profiles support them.
kept.fix: Say 'two other parents into baking' to Chris and 'you and Mark both love coffee, and Chris enjoys it too' to Imani.

kept.what: Mark is 'not into dining' and was placed in a bakery coffee-and-pastries meetup; code found no conflict and his agent accepted.
kept.why: A bakery table is arguably a light form of dining; it is a judgment call whether this touches his dislike.
kept.expected: Nothing required; coffee is his top love and the agent accepted knowingly.

kept.what: The invite to Ron asserts the night is 'friendly and casual, not competitive' [282], and Ron's agent leaned on that assurance when accepting [294], though the event description itself only says 'board game night at a neighbor's table' [198].
kept.why: Ron avoids competitive settings; if the games turn competitive the assurance was the matchmaker's framing rather than a documented feature of the event.
kept.expected: Frame the tone as a suggestion (e.g. 'meant to be casual') rather than a guarantee, or note it in the final message so the group knows Ron prefers low-key play.
kept.fix: Soften 'not competitive' to 'meant to be casual' in the invite and final message to Ron.

kept.what: The matchmaker's rationale says all three members 'also enjoy live music', but Rosa's profile lists no interest in live music.
kept.why: The group reasoning rests partly on an invented shared trait, even though the invites and final messages did not repeat the error.
kept.expected: Rationale should cite only interests actually in the profiles (craft beer for all three; live music for Rachel and Heather only).
kept.fix: Reword the reason to 'three craft-beer lovers, two of whom also enjoy live music'.

kept.what: The matchmaker told Rachel the brewery is 'close by' and Heather it is 'nearby'; both avoid long drives, Rachel is in Downtown and Heather in Lake Sawyer, but the venue's location is not in the log.
kept.why: If the venue is far from either neighborhood the invite would misstate a fact that matters to both people's avoidances; the log cannot confirm either way.
kept.expected: Proximity claims should be verifiable against the venue location.
kept.fix: Include the venue's neighborhood in the proposal or drop the unverified proximity claim.

kept.what: Invites and confirmations describe 'really likes' items as favorites/loves (Ron's photography [114][185], Claire's birding [185]) and tell Noah all three others 'enjoy birds' though Wei lists no birding [119].

kept.what: Headline says 'Four Black Diamond neighbors meet at dawn' though only Ron and Claire live in Black Diamond Ridge (Noah: Downtown, Wei: Morgan Creek), and the 8am start is described as dawn.

kept.what: Confirmations to Noah and Claire name only Ron and Claire / Ron and Noah, leaving Wei unmentioned as a participant.

kept.what: Final messages say Andres and Donna 'both love boating' and Donna/Lauren 'love' running and craft beer, when Donna is only 'up for' boating and craft beer and Lauren only 'up for' running.

kept.what: The final messages say Quinn, Kevin, and Heather 'all love running' and that Heather's 'love of running' is shared, but Heather's profile lists running only as 'is up for'.

kept.expected: Describe shared interests at the intensity the profiles actually state.

kept.what: The matchmaker told Kevin the courts are 'a short trip' and told Heather they are 'close to Lake Sawyer, so no long drive', and Heather's agent repeated 'close by'.
